newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's 1997 GDP growth seen lowest in LatAm.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's 1997 GDP growth seen lowest in LatAm.

text.p: Colombia is likely to show the lowest rate of economic growth in Latin America this year, the country's National Association of Financial Institutions said in a report published Thursday.

The influential financial association said slow growth in Colombia's gross domestic product (GDP) threatened to drive foreign investment away from the country. Colombia's economy posted the strongest economic growth in the region between 1990 and 1995.
Last year Colombia's economy grew 2.08 percent, one of the country's weakest performances in a decade and lower than the 1996 growth rate of every other Latin American nation except Venezuela.
The Colombian government is forecasting 3 percent growth this year, which the association says would fall short of growth in every other country in the region.
The association criticized the government for failure to promote long-term growth and called for tax reform, an overhaul of labor legislation and further privatization.
In the area of tax reform, it recommended a cut in company tax, which it said was one of the highest rates in Latin America and promoted a high rate of tax evasion.
On the plus side, the association praised the government for its management of foreign debt policy.
